hypothesis: Physically consistent local-to-world coordinate transformation reduces wearing-orientation shift, allowing independent IMU motion to correct near-tied primary predictions.

evidence.quaternion_audit: Every thirtieth training clip, 13053 valid readings. Applying wxyz q rotation gives median stationary acceleration [-0.00363,-0.00425,0.98848] g and horizontal norm .07997; inverse gives horizontal .63689.
evidence.prior_work: Earlier multirate skeleton+IMU fusion failed; this is a standalone sensor model and physically verified coordinate-view ablation, without the old branch.

model: 6 InceptionTime-inspired residual Conv1D modules, 16 filters per branch, kernels9/19/39, global average +40-class head; equal parameter count for both views
control: 60 channels formed by duplicating the local five-sensor 6-channel input
candidate: 60 channels formed by concatenating local and quaternion-rotated world inputs
input_contract: Sort device readings by within-clip time; shared linear resampling to256; acceleration in g and angular velocity/180. No absolute time, duration, hardware identity, temperature, battery, firmware, magnetometer or angle features. At least3 sensors with >=4 valid readings.

training.augmentation: shared temporal crop205..256 resized256, iid noise.01
training.held_evaluation: once, final fp16 stored state; bfloat16 compute
training.normalization: fixed physical scaling + batchnorm fitted only on outer train

candidate_integration: on both-primary-valid rows with>=3 valid IMUs, fixed probability blend .9 baseline +.1 sensor; unchanged elsewhere; sensor temperature1; no weight search
scope: Baseline OOF still has target-pretrained upstream contamination; independently trained IMU has held users excluded. Report historical and current paired primary baselines separately.
stopping_rule: No coordinate, fusion-weight, epoch, optimizer or architecture scan using these held outcomes; no test inference unless the gates pass.
